For an integer \(t\ge 2\), consider all integers \(k\ge t\), finite sets \(V\), and families \(\mathcal F\) of \(k\)-element subsets of \(V\) with the following properties. The family is intersecting, meaning that \(F\cap F'\ne\varnothing\) for all \(F,F'\in\mathcal F\). Its covering number is \(t\), where the covering number is the minimum cardinality of a set \(C\subseteq V\) meeting every member of \(\mathcal F\).

In addition, choose a partition \(\mathcal F=\mathcal F_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\mathcal F_t\) into nonempty subfamilies and pairwise disjoint nonempty sets \(X_1,\ldots,X_t\subseteq V\) such that \(X_i\subseteq F\) for every \(F\in\mathcal F_i\). Define
\[
b(t)=\min\sum_{i=1}^{t}\bigl(k-|X_i|\bigr),
\]
where the minimum ranges over all the choices just described, including \(k\) and \(V\).

With \(\log\) denoting the natural logarithm, determine the exact value of
\[
\lim_{\substack{t\to\infty\\t\in\mathbb Z}}\frac{\log b(t)}{\log t}.
\]

The limit is \(\boxed{2}\).

We use the **disjoint-core inequality**: if an intersecting family \(\mathcal H\) has covering number \(s\), and
\[
\mathcal H=\mathcal H_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\mathcal H_s,
\]
where the nonempty families \(\mathcal H_i\) have pairwise disjoint nonempty cores \(A_i\), then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^s\max_{H\in\mathcal H_i}|H\setminus A_i|
   \ge \binom{s}{2}.
\]
Here a core means a set contained in every member of the corresponding subfamily. This is the usual disjoint-core form of the transversal inequality.

Applying this inequality with \(A_i=X_i\), and using uniformity, gives
\[
b(t)\ge \binom{t}{2}.
\]

For completeness, the matching upper bound has a simple construction. Take pairwise disjoint sets
\[
X_1,\ldots,X_t,\qquad |X_i|=t-i+1,
\]
and set \(k=t\). Define
\[
\mathcal F_i=
\left\{
X_i\cup\{x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1}\}:
x_j\in X_j\text{ for }1\le j<i
\right\}.
\]
Every member of \(\mathcal F_i\) has size
\[
(t-i+1)+(i-1)=t.
\]
If \(i<j\), every member of \(\mathcal F_j\) contains a point of \(X_i\), whereas every member of \(\mathcal F_i\) contains all of \(X_i\). Thus the union \(\mathcal F\) is intersecting.

Choosing one point from each \(X_i\) gives a transversal of size \(t\). Conversely, suppose \(|C|<t\), and let \(i\) be the largest index such that \(C\cap X_i=\varnothing\). Such an index exists. For every \(j>i\), the set \(C\) meets \(X_j\), so these blocks account for at least \(t-i\) points of \(C\). Consequently, \(C\) cannot contain any whole block \(X_j\) with \(j<i\), because
\[
|X_j|+(t-i)\ge (t-i+2)+(t-i)>t-1.
\]
Hence we may choose \(x_j\in X_j\setminus C\) for every \(j<i\). The resulting member
\[
X_i\cup\{x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1}\}\in\mathcal F_i
\]
avoids \(C\). Therefore \(\tau(\mathcal F)=t\).

The construction has
\[
\sum_{i=1}^t(k-|X_i|)
=\sum_{i=1}^t(i-1)
=\binom{t}{2}.
\]
Thus \(b(t)=\binom{t}{2}\), and in particular
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\log b(t)}{\log t}
=\lim_{t\to\infty}
\frac{\log\!\bigl(t(t-1)/2\bigr)}{\log t}
=\boxed{2}.
\]
